conviction_note: Read-throughs from peers that printed after ACI's July cut lean negative on identical sales: Kroger slowed to +0.2% and cut its ID guide, Ahold US was hit by SNAP and the IRA, and Costco is taking share. Against that, Kroger held EPS on pharmacy mix, cost savings, tariff refunds and fuel; the $0.33 bar is already -25% y/y and sits inside the July guide; and 12.3% of shares are short at 7.5 days to cover. With +9.4 put skew already pricing the downside, p_up is 47 on an 8% abs move, so the scaled number is -0.48. That matches the findings' sum of -0.5 only roughly, and neither was fitted to the other.
bar: Q2 FY26 (12 weeks to 2026-09-12): adjusted EPS $0.33, revenue $18.83-18.88bn. EPS agrees across two sources: Zacks via Yahoo (2026-10-08, EPS unchanged over 30 days) https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/wall-streets-insights-key-metrics-121519096.html and Investing.com (2026-10-12) https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/albertsons-earnings-up-next-can-aci-edge-turn-around-grocery-93CH-4944664. Company FY26 guide from 2026-07-23: identical sales (1.5)% to (0.5)%, adjusted EBITDA $3.550-3.625bn, adjusted EPS $1.75-1.85 https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001646972/000164697226000041/aciq126earningsrelease.htm. print_vs_bar_pct is measured on revenue. No sourced consensus for Q2 identical sales was found.
positioning_check: 59.5m shares short at the 2026-09-30 settlement = 12.3% of shares outstanding, 7.48 days to cover (equibles.com/stocks/aci/shortinterest, read 2026-10-12, via sweep row). Benzinga shows 15.8% of float and 6.7 days to cover, undated. The short is crowded. Baseline 25d skew is +9.4 vol points, puts bid ('downside paid'); put/call OI is 0.44; 5-day run-up +6.99% into the print after a -21.6% reaction in July; 37.6% off the 52-week high.

findings.finding: Kroger released Q2 on 2026-09-11, after ACI last spoke. For the quarter to 2026-08-15, which overlaps most of ACI's Q2 (Jun 21-Sep 12), identical sales ex-fuel were +0.2%, slowing from about +0.9% in Q1 (H1 +0.6%). Kroger blamed a late-quarter Cyclospora produce pullback (~35bp), egg deflation (~30bp), the generic shift (50-60bp) and IRA Medicare pricing (140bp, larger in H2), and cut its FY ID guide from 1-2% to 0.2-0.8%. The same forces point to ACI's Q2 ID at or below the -1.5% low end of its guide, and to a possible third ID guide trim in a row.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: ACI sells guide cuts hard: -21.6% on the July 2026 FY26 cut and -5.96% on the January 2026 Medicare-related trim. It rose +13.6% in October 2025 on an ID beat and a raised guide. Kroger itself rose ~2% on an ID cut with EPS held.
findings.why_not_priced: If the market fully expected a sub-guide ID print and a guide trim, the EPS consensus would have been revised down after Kroger. Zacks shows it unchanged over 30 days, and Investing.com says EPS estimates rose modestly over 60 days. The stock would also not have run up 7% in five sessions. The put skew does price some of this.
findings.independence: Ahold Delhaize US Q2 (finding 2) and Grocery Dive's account of the Kroger call https://www.grocerydive.com/news/kroger-earnings-second-quarter-2026-grocery-supermarkets/830070/ (the same Kroger event, not counted twice).

findings.finding: Ahold Delhaize US Q2 (reported 2026-08-05): comparable sales ex-gas +0.8%, with SNAP benefit cuts plus egg deflation costing 0.9pt and IRA pharmacy pricing 0.7pt. Ahold said SNAP will weigh through 2026. National SNAP rolls fell 13% y/y to 36.6m in May 2026, and California is among the states still to implement stricter work requirements, a heavy-exposure state for ACI's Safeway and Vons banners.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: ACI's identical sales have driven its reactions: -0.8% ID in Q1 FY26 sat inside a -21.6% day that was driven by the guide. No reaction has been isolated to SNAP.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced. SNAP was public when ACI set its July guide, and its 10-Q cites 'shifts in state and federal assistance programs'. What remains is the chance that California's rollout during ACI's Q2 pushes ID below the guided range. A priced risk would look like an ID consensus below -1.5%, and none is sourced.
findings.independence: SNAP enrollment data https://thegrio.com/2026/08/21/snap-enrollment-drops-work-requirements/ (2026-08-21). This is a proxy: ACI has not quantified SNAP.

findings.finding: Costco US comparable sales ex-gas and FX were +8.0% for the five weeks to 2026-10-04 (released 2026-10-07; Labor Day added ~50bp). That is continued share capture by clubs while traditional grocers run near zero or negative ID.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None is specific to ACI. Share loss shows up in ID, and ID moves ACI mainly through the guide.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced as a long-running trend. It adds only a little to the read that traditional-grocer ID stayed weak through September.
findings.independence: Kroger ID +0.2% (finding 1) points the same way from a different source. This is a proxy.

findings.finding: Kroger held its FY EPS ($5.10-5.30) and FIFO operating profit guide through the ID cut, with Q2 adjusted EPS +5% y/y and FIFO gross margin +13bp. It credited favourable pharmacy mix (the IRA lifts the margin rate even as it cuts sales), sourcing, tariff refunds and strong fuel. ACI's Q1 also showed IRA-related pharmacy margin improvement. The read for ACI's EPS against a $0.33 bar that is already -25% y/y is positive.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: ACI EPS beats have not been enough when the guide moved: Q2 FY25 beat $0.44 vs $0.40 with a raised ID guide and rose +13.6%. Q1 FY26 missed $0.42 vs $0.54 and fell -21.6%, but on the guide cut.
findings.why_not_priced: The ACI EPS consensus did not move after Kroger showed the margin offsets (Zacks: unchanged over 30 days), and put skew is +9.4. If the market had priced an EPS hold, the skew would be flatter and estimates would have risen. The bar sits inside the July guide, so an EPS-in-line or small-beat outcome is partly expected, which keeps this small.
findings.independence: ACI's own Q1 FY26 release notes 'pharmacy margin improvement related to the IRA' https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001646972/000164697226000041/aciq126earningsrelease.htm. This shares the Kroger document with finding 1; finding 1 is the top-line reading of it and this is the margin reading.

findings.finding: Leadership reset ahead of the print: Meg Whitman was made Executive Chair with $8.9m of RSUs (8-K 2026-09-09), the CFO handed over to an interim CFO (Cody Perdue) on 2026-09-30, three directors join effective 2026-10-14, and the EVP of M&A received a retention RSU grant on 2026-09-08. A first print under a new chair and interim CFO raises the odds of a reset or a conservative guide alongside the ACI Edge update.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None isolated for leadership changes. The July 2026 CFO retirement was announced the same day as the guide cut (-21.6%).
findings.why_not_priced: The facts are public. The inference that a reset becomes more likely is not reflected in an unchanged EPS consensus. This is inference, so it is small.
findings.independence: Whitman 8-K https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1646972/000164697226000054/aci-20260908.htm and Form 4 (Moriarty) https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1646972/000162828026061402/wk-form4_1789074141.xml. Same company, different documents.

findings.finding: Crowded short into a low bar: 12.3% of shares short at 7.48 days to cover (2026-09-30 settlement), against an EPS bar already cut 25% y/y and inside the guide. A held FY guide could force covering. The 5-day run-up of +7% suggests some covering has already started.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: When the guide held or rose (October 2025), ACI rose +13.6%. When it was cut, it fell 6-22%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced through the 5-day run-up. Put skew at +9.4 shows the option market is not paying for the squeeze side.
findings.independence: Benzinga short-interest page (15.8% of float, 6.7 days to cover, undated), cited via the sweep row.

findings.finding: Southern California UFCW pharmacists at Vons, Albertsons and Pavilions have worked on an expired contract since March 1 and authorised a strike in July. On 2026-09-04 they urged customers by email and text (~50,000 contacts) to transfer prescriptions ahead of a possible strike. That is a small risk to pharmacy scripts late in Q2 and to Q3 commentary.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None. A 2025 grocery-worker strike threat was settled with no measurable print effect.
findings.why_not_priced: Local labour news that no preview mentions. It is tiny relative to ACI's ~$80bn of sales.
findings.independence: Strike authorisation reported by NBC Palm Springs https://www.nbcpalmsprings.com/2026/07/17/southern-california-supermarket-pharmacists-vote-to-authorize-strike-amid-contract-dispute

Washington State opioid bench trial (began 2026-07-13; statute-of-limitations defence struck 2026-07-30). No verdict found. It is excluded from the $774m national settlement framework.

baseline_tension: The negative top-line findings agree with the +9.4 put skew and the stock's 38% drawdown, so they are mostly priced. The positives (EPS-margin read, crowded short) cut against the skew but agree with the +7% 5-day run-up. Net, the set is close to balanced with a slight negative lean.
lessons_applied: Lesson 7 (crowded short; the negatives agree with the strong put skew, so they are likely priced): shrank the Kroger ID read -1.5 to -1.0, SNAP -0.7 to -0.5 and the pharmacist item -0.2 to -0.1; p_up moved 45 to 47
Lesson 5 (proxies small): SNAP further to -0.4 and Costco -0.3 to -0.2, both kept as filed proxies
Lesson 6 (inside the guide): SNAP was known when ACI set its July ID range, which adds to the shrink above (one cut, not stacked); the $0.33 EPS bar is two-source verified and sits inside the guide
Lesson 1/2 (fact is not reaction; one-offs): the Kroger margin read (tariff refunds, fuel) moved +1.0 to +0.8, because ACI has not paid for EPS when the guide moves
Lesson 3 (own caveat): the leadership-reset inference moved -0.5 to -0.4, since its own text says the facts are public
